Vistra gained 3.7% to $139.59 ahead of Friday's results, while Autodesk gave back 2.2% to $252.32 after Monday's 3.3% gain; no company-specific news was found for those two.

explainer.meaning: Sales of chips that go into the big server farms where AI models are trained and run, the market Nvidia leads.

stories.headline: AMD rises ~6.5% after hours as it guides Q4 revenue to about $17bn; data-centre sales nearly double

impacts.why: Meta is among the customers running workloads on AMD's initial Helios systems [1].

sources.title: AMD Q3 earnings: Revenue rises 45% to $13.4B
AMD Forecasts 66% Q4 Growth on AI Chip Demand: Rapid Earnings Reaction

stories.summary: AMD reported third-quarter revenue of $13.4bn (+45%) with data-centre revenue of $8.5bn (+97%), and guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17bn, roughly 66% growth. CEO Lisa Su said demand for its Instinct AI chips and EPYC server chips continued to strengthen, and the company named Anthropic, Meta, Microsoft, OpenAI and Oracle as running workloads on its first Helios rack systems. The shares rose about 6.5% after hours (not a confirmed close).

explainer.meaning: AI software that takes actions by itself, such as sending emails or changing systems, which creates new security risks if it goes wrong.

stories.headline: CrowdStrike buys two AI-security start-ups for $495m and launches an AI 'kill switch'; ISPY falls 2%

impacts.why: ISPY closed 3,533p, down 2.0% on the day [2]; CrowdStrike itself rose about 2% early on the deals [1].

stories.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to buy Fiddler AI and Dreadnode for a combined $495m (per the Wall Street Journal), adding tools to monitor AI systems and test them for weaknesses, and unveiled a 'kill switch' to shut down misbehaving AI agents. Its shares rose about 2% in early trading. Your cyber ETF still fell 2.0% in London to 3,533p, extending a run of declines for the sector.

explainer.meaning: US elections held halfway through a president's term that decide control of Congress, which affects tax and spending laws.

stories.summary: Wall Street finished mixed on midterm election day: the Nasdaq rose 0.83% to 25,372 and the S&P 500 0.36% to 7,569 on the chip rebound, while the Dow fell 0.38% as Apple dropped about 1.9% on a disappointing margin forecast. VWRP closed down 0.86% at £140.20 in London, which shuts before the US rally built; it is now 4.7% below its 6 Oct high. Palantir and Shopify fell after their results.

stories.summary: Gold futures fell about 1.5% to around $3,912 an ounce and silver nearly 4% by early afternoon in New York, TheStreet reported, after an early gain toward $3,966 that Kitco linked to Iran tensions and the midterms. Kitco says expectations of a Fed rate rise in December are limiting gold's recovery. SGLN closed down 1.0% at 5,680p in London.

explainer.meaning: A narrow sea route off Iran that a large share of the world's oil tankers pass through.

Stock market today: Dow slips, S&P and Nasdaq gain as chip stocks rally, focus shifts to midterm elections

stories.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island, described by officials as defensive moves to stop attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent rose early but later slipped about 1% to around $103-104 on hopes for US-Iran talks, Yahoo Finance said. US petrol and diesel hit Election Day record highs of $4.14 and $6.29 a gallon.

explainer.meaning: A monthly US report on job vacancies and hiring, used to judge how tight the jobs market is.

stories.headline: US job openings steady at 7.5m; 10-year yield near 4.95% with jobs report and midterm results ahead

sources.title: Stock market today: Dow slips, S&P and Nasdaq gain as chip stocks rally, focus shifts to midterm elections
Gold gains, silver slips as U.S. midterms and Iran strikes unsettle markets

stories.summary: US job openings were 7.5 million in September with hiring little changed, a 'low hire, low fire' market, Yahoo Finance reported, and the 10-year Treasury yield ended near 4.95%. Kitco notes core PCE inflation at 3.1% and expectations of a December Fed rate rise. Prediction markets gave Democrats a 76% chance of winning both chambers of Congress, with results due overnight; the October jobs report is on Friday.

stories.headline: Grab raises its 2026 profit guide after record quarter; all three businesses now profitable

impacts.why: Full-year EBITDA guide raised to $790-800m and financial services reached profitability [1]; shares up ~3.9% after hours to $2.97 [2].
Management plans deliberate extra spending in Q4 on driver supply and new products [3].

sources.title: Grab Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results, Raises Full-Year Guidance
Grab Holdings Q3 Results Climb, Lifts FY26 Outlook; Shares Gain
Earnings call transcript: Grab posts first all-segment profit in Q3 2026

stories.summary: Grab's revenue rose 27% to $1.11bn and adjusted EBITDA jumped 73% to a record $237m, with financial services turning a profit for the first time. It lifted its full-year adjusted EBITDA guide to $790-800m (from $720-740m) and revenue to $4.15-4.20bn, and has bought back $400m of shares since September. Net profit was only $18m after a $57m fair-value loss. The shares closed 5.5% higher on Monday before the release and rose about 3.9% further in after-hours trading.

Monday's final figures were weaker than first reported: the Nasdaq fell 1.07% and the S&P 500 0.51%, while the Dow rose 0.4%. Apple fell 2.8% after hours on a weaker margin forecast.

stories.summary: Gold recovered towards $3,950 from a yearly low near $3,870 as the oil slump eased inflation worries and pulled US yields lower. Strong US factory data lifted bets on a December Fed rate rise, which weighs on gold. Your gold ETC (SGLN) closed 1.65% higher on Monday.

explainer.meaning: Markets have already adjusted prices for an expected event, so it moves them less when it happens.

stories.headline: Bank of England set to raise rates to 4% on Thursday, its first rise since 2023

sources.title: BoE Preview: Bank Set to Lift Rates to 4% as Inflation Bites

stories.summary: Investors and most analysts expect a quarter-point rise to 4% at noon Thursday, after UK inflation climbed to 3.5% in September with oil above $100. A rise is largely priced in, so attention will be on how the committee votes. Ten-year gilt yields were recently around 5.31%.

explainer.meaning: One hundredth of a percentage point, so 2 basis points is 0.02%.

sources.title: Asian stocks retreat ahead of US midterms, oil steadies

stories.summary: Brent crude rose 0.5% to about $105.30 in Asian trade after Monday's drop of more than 7% on US-Iran peace talk reports. The US 10-year Treasury yield rose 2 basis points to 4.91%. The pound was a little firmer at about $1.34.

topline: Results landed well: Fabrinet closed +15.5% at $363.33 and Grab +9.1% at $3.12 after their beat-and-raise reports; JPMorgan raised targets on both.
Chips rebounded: Nasdaq +0.83%, now about 8.0% below its 6 Oct high; Nvidia +2.3%, Meta +2.4% (planning a $20-25bn bond sale), Amazon +2.0%. AMD up ~6.5% after hours on a ~$17bn Q4 guide.
London closed before the US rally: VWRP -0.9% (4.7% below its high), cyber ETF ISPY -2.0%, gold SGLN -1.0%; grid ETF FGRD +1.2% and Vistra +3.7%.
Oil whipsawed on reported US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island; US 10-year yield near 4.95%.
Midterm results come overnight; Bank of England (rise to 4% expected) Thursday, Vistra results and US jobs Friday.
